title: Inequalities
description: Solving and representing linear inequalities, compound inequalities, and graphical inequalities on a coordinate plane.

notes.heading: Solving Linear Inequalities
notes.body: Solve like equations, but with one critical exception: when multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number, REVERSE the inequality sign. Example: −2x < 6 → x > −3.

notes.heading: Number Line Representation
notes.body: Open circle (○) = value NOT included (< or >). Filled circle (●) = value IS included (≤ or ≥). Arrow extends in the direction of all satisfying values. Compound inequality: −1 < x ≤ 5 shown with open circle at −1, filled at 5, segment shaded between.

notes.heading: Compound Inequalities
notes.body: Solve by applying operations to all three parts. Example: −2 ≤ 3x+1 < 10 → −3 ≤ 3x < 9 → −1 ≤ x < 3. Solutions include all values from −1 to 3 (including −1, excluding 3).

notes.heading: Graphical Inequalities
notes.body: Draw the boundary line. Use solid if ≤ or ≥ (boundary included), dashed if < or > (boundary excluded). Test a point (e.g., (0,0)) to determine which side to shade. Multiple inequalities give a feasible region.

notes.heading: Rearranging Inequalities with Variables on Both Sides
notes.body:
Solving inequalities with terms on both sides follows the same rules as equations, with extra care for negative coefficients.

📌 Definition
An inequality with variables on both sides, such as $5x - 3 \le 2x + 9$, still has a range of solutions rather than a single value.

🔑 How it works
1. Collect variable terms on one side and numbers on the other.
2. If you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.
3. Simplify to the form $x \; \text{symbol} \; \text{value}$.

💡 Worked Example
Solve $7 - 3x > 13$.
Subtract 7: $-3x > 6$.
Divide by $-3$ and reverse: $x < -2$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Treat $>$ and $<$ the same way as $=$ until the final step.
• Only reverse the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
• A solution like $x < -2$ means every number less than $-2$ works, not just $-2$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to reverse the sign when dividing by a negative. For example, $-4x \ge 20$ becomes $x \le -5$, not $x \ge -5$.

notes.heading: Writing and Solving Word Problems
notes.body:
Inequalities are used to describe real situations that involve a limit, minimum, or maximum.

📌 Definition
A word problem gives a relationship in words that can be translated into an inequality using phrases such as 'at least' ($\ge$), 'at most' ($\le$), 'more than' ($>$), and 'fewer than' ($<$).

🔑 How it works
1. Choose a variable for the unknown quantity.
2. Translate the words into symbols.
3. Solve the inequality.
4. Interpret the answer in context.

💡 Worked Example
A taxi charges a £3 booking fee plus £2 per mile. You have at most £25. How many miles can you travel?
Let $m$ be the number of miles.
$$3 + 2m \le 25$$
$$2m \le 22$$
$$m \le 11$$
You can travel at most $11$ miles.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• 'At most' and 'no more than' mean $\le$.
• 'At least' and 'no less than' mean $\ge$.
• The final answer should be given in a sentence, not just as $x \le \dots$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using $<$ instead of $\le$ when the phrase includes 'or equal to', such as 'at most 12'.

notes.heading: Special Solution Sets
notes.body:
Some inequalities simplify to statements that are always true or always false.

📌 Definition
The solution set of an inequality is the collection of all values that make it true. It can be all real numbers, no real numbers, or a bounded interval.

🔑 How it works
If the variable disappears:
• A true statement, such as $5 > 2$, means the solution is all real numbers.
• A false statement, such as $3 < 1$, means there is no solution.

💡 Worked Example
Solve $2x + 4 < 2x + 10$.
Subtract $2x$: $4 < 10$.
This is always true, so the solution is all real numbers.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $x > x$ has no solution.
• $x \le x$ is true for all real numbers.
• On a number line, all real numbers is drawn as the entire line.

✅ Check
Substitute any value into the original inequality. If the variable has disappeared and the statement is true, every value works.
